Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink Let’s just say. . . I’m not “squealing with laughter” as it shows on the listing in several places.

First of all. . . This is NOT a pretty pig. It’s kind of “odd” because the color is different in the pictures (the picture of the girl holding it makes it look white with a little tan and black splotches. . . which it is not). The one that I received looks like different shades of tan with some dark splotches. Not the least bit pink. . . not the least bit attractive. I understand that not all pigs are pink in real life. . . and not all pings are “pretty”. . . but when you’re making a toy, then the majority of the time they are pink. . . and they should be at least “not-ugly”, which this one is. . . ugly.

The pictures show the pig standing. This pig does not stand. It lays flat down, with the legs forward. There is nothing stiff in the legs so that it can stand, and it’s obviously made to lay flat.

The “puppet part”. There is a “slit” in the bellow where you put four fingers. You have to find the holes for the fingers for the two front legs. Then you use two fingers to move the mouth up-and-down. Not the easiest thing to do.

The pig “grunts” when you squeeze the “rump” part of the pig. Again, not the best design, in my opinion.

There is a tag that shows that this pig won the 2014 “plush toy” award, which I find very hard to believe.

Finally. . . This is a Made in China toy. . . At the current price it’s WAY too expensive for Made in China.

Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players This is a very cute concept and something out-of-the-ordinary for a board game! The object of the game is to make it out with the least amount of goo on your shoe. This is represented by actual pieces of putty that you place on the board and squish with your pawn as you land on a square (thus sticking the goo to your, erm, shoe).
My kids really enjoyed it, but I can't help feeling like there are some design flaws that could have been prevented. For example, the spinner needs to be deconstructed to put away in the box. The way the board folds (see picture), the crease is over the spinner area, and with the bars on the spinner (which I like, as it looks like a playground toy) won't fit, which means you have to totally take that apart and rebuilt it each time. On that note, it isn't much of a spinner at all, but just a wheel. There is no clicker or arrow that sticks out to slow it down as it spins... it basically spins until momentum from your push wears out, sort of like spinning a top. It takes a while to finally stop on its own, which makes the game feel like it is moving slowly. I was very tempted to just stop it manually a few times, but that might bring up the possibility of cheating.
Meanwhile, I wish the goo had more colors, or at least colors that matched the shoes in the game. I can say on the positive note, the goo is very kid friendly!
My daughter lost one of the colors and it turns out she was SITTING on it and it was all stuck in her dress. I suddenly had flashbacks of when silly putty got stuck on her clothing and bed and we had to toss them both because it never came off... but this stuff comes off! It easily rolls into balls with your fingers and comes right off clothing in the process. So, definitely some extra points for that! I just wish the game board and spinner were designed a little better, that would make it a lot more fun to play (and put away!).

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Blocks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler, and they have soft parts! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit

Asmodee Hit Z Road This is a very silly game, despite the theme. Not a gory or cartoonish zombie game, it really could be almost anything in place of them: Mad Max-style marauders, for instance. What's nice about that is, if you're anything like me, and you're totally over all types of zombie games, you will still be able to play Hit Z Road.

This game is really a push your luck dice rolling game with auctions. You're trying to survive until the end of the road, and you need to make some meaningful choices along the way that could make your journey much easier, or much more daring. There is some player elimination, but it's not one of those "you can die on the first turn" types of eliminations - our earliest death was about 10 minutes before the end of the game.

I think a lot of people will find the artwork on this game to be fantastic, and I have to admit that it is daring, different, and one of the most unique looking games out there. While I can admire the work that went into it, the art just doesn't appeal to me.

The name, by the way, might be one of the worst in the history of board gaming.

Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll As a longtime Barbie collector, I'm always curious when a new Barbie doll uses a gimmick that was popular years ago. In this case, the Barbie Hairtastic Color Styling doll offers the same "color magic" idea that made a 1966 Barbie doll a best-seller. The concept is similar - wet the doll's hair and you can change her hair color using a simple brush and a "foil clip".

This doll comes with a chair, water brush, comb, water bowl (for rinsing the brush), eight "foil" cards (purple, orange and pink), a set of three Barbie hairties, and a styling "foil clip".

The box makes the color transfer seem easy, but actually it takes a bit of work. The instructions say "wet the hair generously" so if you do this with a child, be sure to have a newspaper or towel around so that the doll's hair and the dyes don't stain your table. The foil clip comes already loaded with an orange card, so I tried that first.

The results were mixed. I had to run the clip up and down the hair a few times before the color started to show. I also had to reapply the wet brush several times even though the hair seemed wet enough. Finally, the orange color streak came out bright and strong. Then I tried the purple dye, and the color was faint and weak. I added more water and tried again, but the purple dye failed to transfer a rich color. Not sure why this is.

Contrary to the box claims, the foils can't be reused. It's low-tech - a swatch of watercolor paint on the back of a foil card. When some of the dye from the purple card failed to transfer, I simply took the card out of the clip and rubbed the card itself into the hair. This was sloppy but it did the job better.

The chair has a suction cup, which is a wonderful and long-needed feature. Barbie sat snugly in her chair and it remained firmly anchored while styling. I wish all Barbie chairs had something like this.

Lastly, the instructions don't mention how long the dye will last, only that it comes off with water. Good, but I found that the dye stained my hands and clothing. If a child does this, be prepared. The clip idea is good, but it doesn't fully prevent the process from getting messy.

Overall, it's a decent toy but once the dyes run out, you'd be left with an ordinary Barbie doll.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome I figured the Fisher-Price Power Wheels Dune Racer would be a great way to keep my nieces' occupied when they visit. It certainly made them very happy when they saw it! Over all, it's a great power cart and an improvement on the one they have at home, but there are one or two minor issues.
It was delivered in a large box, and since is a 'some assembly required' type of toy, some components were not secured in the box. These parts were in plastic packed within thin foam, along with heavier parts, and had been bounced around in shipping. Because of the way the racer was packed, this meant that there were some scratches on some of the smaller chromed plastic pieces. A minor detail, but some people might not be happy to have a toy arrive in less than pristine shape (also, know that a VERY large box may be just left on your porch or by your garage).
Assembly took the boyfriend about 45 minutes using a screw gun with no issues... but he's pretty good about putting things together. Might take some others a bit longer.
While we tested the battery and found out that it had a little charge right out of the box, for a full charge, you pretty much will have to charge it overnight (about eighteen hours). So yeah, there's a bit of delayed fun-time with the toy. Might be some disappointed kiddies if they see it and then find out they can't do much more than sit in it for about a day.
The decals were tough to peel from the sheet. The wax paper was peeling off along with the sticker due to how thin the stickers were, and they were cut too deep into the backing paper. All in all they were a bit of a pain to put onto the racer - might not be worth it to put them on at all (not sure my nieces care about them, to be honest).
Another minor issue is that the gas pedal is in the middle of the cart, causing the driver to stretch a little to reach (especially when you add that you can't move the seat forward). The shifter was also in the center, as well as directly under the driver’s right knee (at least for my nieces, who are a little more than four years old). So when they were touching the gas pedal, it would sometime shift gears on them, between reverse, low and high. They seem to be learning to be more careful, but still, something to be concerned about when this happened, especially in reverse when they would hit the gas, and their leg would bump the shifter into forwards, causing the cart to lurch in that direction.
A nice thing about the Fisher-Price racer is that it goes well on both grass and on hills with a 30 degree angle. Compared to an older power wheels toddler 6v that the girls have that couldn't manage going up hills, they're having so much more fun (and want to take it home). The seat is comfortable and the racer looks great (scratches aside).
There is no 'brake' to the racer, but once the foot is removed from the gas pedal, it stops.
All in all, the racer is a hit and I'm sure the girls will be begging to come over to use it. One or two features could be better designed (I have to wonder if it's to fit to older kids as well to younger), but on the whole, it's a very nice cart that kids should be able to enjoy for a couple of years (depending on their age).
Overall the kids love it and have a blast with it. Giving 4 stars because of packing, QC issues, and some ergo issues.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

Replogle Aragon 12" Desktop World Globe, Raised Relief, Up-to-Date Cartography, Made in USA (Blue Ocean) The review always asks: What did you use this product for?
Well, when we watch the network news at night, I never know, exactly, where the places are that are in the news.
When I'm introduced to a new person who has an accent I just can't place, and when I ask them where they're from and they answer with the the name of a country, that I'm not familiar with, let alone the continent it resides on, I feel like an ass.
And admit it, when you play Jeopardy (and 90% of the world plays Jeopardy) your palms start to sweat when the category is Capitals Of The World.
And you go into overdrive when the Final Answer is: What peninsula (peninsula?) is where the historic treaty of peace (what?) was signed in 2001 between the United States and the Republic of Whatever (OMG).
This replogle globe, which is Made in the United States, is not only beautiful but it holds lots of information. The Legend denotes swamps from canals and shipping routes. You just can't believe what you can "read" on a globe. If you want to know where they are and you are in this world, buy a globe. Buy this one.
Can you name at least three countries that survive Ukraine?
I rest my case.

Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored Excellent game for toddlers and preschoolers! This collaborative game (everyone works as a team) is so easy to learn and play. For two to four players, the game board is three piece, six foot long puzzle. After you set up the board, everyone has a marker. There are about ten magnifying glasses, a cardboard boat, six cardboard pieces of food, cards, a spinner, and a timer. The goal? Everyone has to make it to the boat and the boat has to make it to Picnic Island before the pigs eat all the food. The youngest person goes first.

Each player spins the spinner. The arrow lands on either a Move, a Bug, or a Pig. If you spin to a Move, you move your marker that many spaces and the next player goes. If you spin to a Pig, the Pigs "eat" one picnic food item and you take one food items away and spin again. If you spin to a bug, you pull a card. When you pull the card, you have to look throughout the game board for those items (almost Where's Waldo style). For example, if you pull a card with pictures of "balloons", you set the timer and look all around the game board for balloons. You use the magnifying glasses to mark that you've found one. When the timer is up you count how many "balloons" you found and all players move that many spaces. So if you found three balloons, everyone moves three spaces. Once everyone lands on the boat, everyone takes turns to spin to move the boat to Picnic Island. So long as the pigs haven't eaten all the food, everyone wins!

This game is a great concept for kids who have issues with winning and losing. Especially at 3 and 4 years of age when other skills like patience, taking turns, and working together are my main focus for my son rather than learning to be a gracious loser (I hope to teach him this later). Focusing and patience are the skills that this game builds as my son loves being a helper and the idea that he is helping for everyone to win actually helps him to focus and be a little more patient. The game also helps with counting and memory. I am pleasantly surprised by this game and I highly recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It Toddler Toy and Game (5 players) for Boys and Girls Age 3 and Up - A Fun Preschool Board Game,Multi-colored

DUPLO blocks are intended for very young builders, and are much larger than regular LEGO blocks. Thus this “Frozen” ice castle set lacks the detail of the regular [[ASIN:B07TB4WCJM LEGO “Frozen” ice palace]] (see photos). But this DUPLO set has a light brick!

The light brick is powered by 3 button cell batteries (pre-installed). When you press the button on the brick, it cycles through a series of colors for a short time, then stops automatically. By repeatedly pressing the button, you can get all white lights; or all blue, red, yellow, green, purple, orange lights. The batteries are replaceable, but you will need a small Phillips head screwdriver to open the light brick. The batteries are NOT accessible to small children.

In comparison to the regular LEGO set, the other great thing about this DUPLO set is the size of the play figures. Elsa, Anna, and Olaf are much larger than regular LEGO mini-figures, so they’re more fun to play with or display. Elsa and Anna have skirts with elastic waists that go on over the plastic figures. Elsa has a sparkly cape, and Anna has a dark red cloak. Olaf is just himself!

It’s kind of amazing, how much the look and feel of the LEGO “Frozen” ice palace set is retained in this simplified DUPLO set.

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition I very much liked the original edition of Werewords (essentially the same game as Insider), and this is the same game, but there's more of it.

Werewords is a lot like "20 questions". Players ask yes/no questions in an attempt to identify a word that could be anything from "spatula" to "Mjollnir". One player is a werewolf, who knows the word already, and is attempting to guide the players with their questioning closer to the actual word without them figuring out that they know the word already. They win if players can identify the word, but do not know which among them is the werewolf. If they do identify the werewolf, then the werewolf can also identify the "seer" player (another with information about the word).

The deluxe edition contains a few additional roles for players. If you already have the other version of this game, I don't think you need to own this version unless you're a completionist. If you don't own any versions of this game, I think it's quite good.

My concern remains the same as before - the app for this game is good, and it doesn't appear to be going anywhere, but if you don't want to run an app while playing this game, then I totally understand, and this game will not be for you at all. I think the app does a good job of balancing the words against one another, creating the ability to discern easy from very difficult words, but the same effect could have been accomplished with cards. I would prefer the cards as well, but the app has the advantage of saving shelf space and also having a larger directory of words. In the end, it's a toss up, but if you don't mind the app, then this is the best possible edition of the game to get.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition

Harry Potter Hogwarts Battle Cooperative Deck Building Card Game | Official Harry Potter Licensed Merchandise | Harry Potter Board Game | Great Gift for Harry Potter Fans | Harry Potter Movie artwork Great fun. Nice cooperative game to play with others to avoid hurt feelings, players "out of the game", and to make things feel low-stakes and casual. You never really rely on others players, it's just that some players can help each other out when possible, but no one loses before anyone else. You all lose at once.

There aren't any story events from the books during each year. As you progress through years, your character cards swap out for older portraits and new enemies and spells are introduced, but your starting character spells never change. You always have to rebuild the deck and gain low level spells even in later years, which seems pretty silly. The strategy can be dumbed down after a while and it really just depends on who the starting villains you get dealt are. You could spend as long as you want building your deck if you get someone like Crabbe and Goyle in the first round.

Dont expect this to be story-rich or something. Seems to just be harry potter themed, in the sense that this could really be almost any other story or universe that has multiple books or a serialized progression and it would also have worked fine. They just happened to pick Harry Potter. That could be a good thing however, since you essentially need zero harry potter knowledge to play.

text_fidelity_a: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage I have been a Barbie fan since I was a child, many years ago. My now 16 year old daughter was a huge fan when she was young. I even have several "in the box" collector Barbies. The Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage just doesn't seem as high quality as the many Barbie products I have purchased over the years. It's definitely not a collector's item. The price is decent and you get a complete set of a doll, unicorn, and carriage. The plastic carriage flexes when you apply pressure. It doesn't feel like it's going to easily break, but it's not as rigid as other Barbie products. The carriage door opens and closes.  The wheels rotate easily and give a pretty smooth ride. The details on the carriage are nice. There are lots of textures to make it more realistic.  The unicorn is a sturdier plastic piece. The doll has the rigid, no bend legs. Her facial details are what you expect on Barbies. She has a removable crown. Her top is molded plastic and not removable. Her skirt is a cute, candy print fabric, but the material itself is stiff and doesn't flow or move. In fact, I don't like the skirt at all. Overall, it's an attractive looking set, but the quality is disappointing. With all that said, I think young Barbie fans would probably still enjoy it.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion

Monster High Monster Maker In my opinion, kids are born these days innately knowing how to handle technology with their little hands. We first used the [[ASIN:B00IVFCD0Q Monster High Monster Maker]] with an eight year old who guided me through each step. I had already downloaded the software for using on my computer, had installed the included AA batteries, and connected the printer cable. His approach was very different than mine because he wanted to print his design on all the legs, then the arms, then the heads. I wanted to do each of the three dolls as a single being. By inserting the pens which actually can be used to draw freehand, the design is drawn directly onto the doll parts and if you don't like the outcome or grow tired of it, they are erasable. My only complaint about this kit is that two wig caps are included and a single rooted wig whereas the rooted wigs are far superior. The shoes are pretty cute and the dresses are very simple. When I have time, I'll put together some more of the little dresses with fabric scraps.

Keeping all the small parts together is well contained with this set and the [[ASIN:B00LOR4Z3Q Monster High Monster Maker Primary Extension Pack]] is an affordable addition. Because the ink is fairly light when applied to the dolls, there has not been residual color remaining after we've used the eraser to clean them up for refreshed designs. This is a very smart "toy" that is capable of entertaining small groups of children as well as a single designer. By having more dolls on hand, it's a great tool for a birthday party, especially when each child can leave with a doll of their own that they have designed.
text_fidelity_b: Monster High Monster Maker

text_fidelity_a:
Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive First the good.
I shot light rapids in this puppy on the Blackfoot River in Montana. The collapsibility makes it easy to bring even if you don't have a pickup truck. You could put several in a compact car. You can blow it up with your own lungs in under five minutes, easily. It has good back support, very comfortable. The nylon cover protects from rocks. The foot rest and low profile give unparalleled maneuverability in rapids. You can get your arms deeper into the water than a traditional tube and the brace your feet on the foot rest to keep your seat when the ride gets wild. The handles allow you to stay in when it gets hectic. I got dumped once and because I was holding the handles, I was able to spin in a downhill rapid and shove it underwater and back under my tuchas to regain my seat.
It has all the advantages of an innertube and a kayak with the comfort of a recliner. The cup holder is also handy.
The bad:
The mesh is flimsy. All they need to do is use the stuff that more common blue and white float tubes use and they have a far better product. I got two small holes going over rocks. That doesn't happen with the blue and white tubes.
Fortunately, I can sew. I'm going to get some better mesh and pimp my floaty!
text_fidelity_b: Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive
